what_its_for: Levothyroxine replaces or provides thyroid hormone that your thyroid gland is not making enough of. It is most commonly used to treat an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It helps relieve symptoms like tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold, dry skin, and slow thinking. It may also be used to treat certain thyroid conditions like goiter or thyroid cancer.
how_to_take: Take levothyroxine by mouth, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast or your first meal of the day. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you to. If you use the liquid capsule form (Tirosint), swallow it whole.
dosing: Your doctor will choose the dose that is right for you based on your age, weight, and blood test results. Most adults start with a low dose that is slowly adjusted over time. Common adult doses range from 25 mcg to 200 mcg once daily. Never change your dose on your own. Your doctor will check your thyroid levels with regular blood tests to make sure your dose is correct.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still morning or early in the day and you have not eaten yet. If it is close to your next dose time or you have already eaten a full meal, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time the following morning. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor if you miss several doses in a row.
storage: Store levothyroxine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking levothyroxine at the same time as antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, or multivitamins — these can block your body from absorbing the medication properly. Take these products at least 4 hours apart from levothyroxine. Avoid eating high-fiber foods, soy products, or foods high in calcium right after taking your dose. Do not stop taking levothyroxine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well. Avoid switching between different brands without checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as different brands may be absorbed differently.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, severe headache, tremors or shaking, feeling extremely nervous, anxious, or irritable, excessive sweating, unusual weight loss, muscle weakness, vomiting or diarrhea, hair loss that is getting worse, swelling in your legs or ankles, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms of low thyroid do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some improvement in your symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks, but it often takes 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit of levothyroxine. Your doctor will check your thyroid hormone levels with a blood test about 6 to 8 weeks after starting or changing your dose. Most people need to take levothyroxine for the rest of their life, so it is important to take it every day even when you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults: Older patients are usually started on a lower dose to reduce the risk of heart-related side effects. Pregnant women: It is very important to continue taking levothyroxine during pregnancy. Your dose may need to be increased. Contact your doctor as soon as you find out you are pregnant. Children: Dosing is based on the child's weight and age and will be adjusted as the child grows. Regular blood tests are especially important for children. People with heart disease: Levothyroxine is started at a very low dose and increased slowly to protect the heart. Always tell your doctor about all health conditions and medications you are taking.
